title: NoSQL and the BASE trade-off

kcs.statement: NoSQL is a family of non-relational data models (key-value, document, wide-column, graph); many NoSQL stores trade joins and multi-record transactions for flexible schemas and built-in partitioning, but some offer transactions and strongly consistent reads, so guarantees must be checked per store.

BASE (basically available, soft state, eventually consistent) is an optional design approach that favours answering during failures and letting replicas converge later; it is a choice some stores make, not a property of every NoSQL store nor the opposite of ACID.

problem_ideas: Sort eight features (likes, wallet balance, product catalog, seat booking, view counts, sessions, audit log, chat history) into 'needs multi-record transactions' and 'eventual consistency is fine'
A like counter shows 1,203 on one device and 1,201 on another for two seconds: explain why a BASE-style store allows it
Name what you may lose when moving a users table from SQL to a key-value store, and how to check whether the chosen store keeps it
An interviewer says 'NoSQL scales, SQL doesn't': give the nuanced answer, covering sharded SQL and transactional NoSQL
Explain soft state using a shopping cart replicated across two regions
List three NoSQL stores you know, the family each belongs to, and whether it offers transactions
